message:
Amara, Chidi and Dalia, chill holding needs a steady cool moist box avoiding rot and cold damage.

Hold target in the assumed chill and humidity concept (C6) is five degrees Celsius and eighty five to ninety five percent Relative Humidity, where Relative Humidity (RH) means moist air fraction, following high-humidity storage (E18) and chilling injury warning below about thirteen to sixteen degrees Celsius (E19).

Box uses 100 millimetre polyurethane insulation (C4), where Polyurethane (PU) means rigid foam insulation, with conductivity zero point zero two three watts per metre kelvin (E27) and zero point zero two two watts per metre kelvin (E28), giving about zero point two two watts per square metre kelvin, as drawn for crates and fan flow with drain in the cold room section sketch (E32).

Amara, your eight kilowatt hour assumption for 8kWh per day load at 5 peak sun hours (E16) is high for steady holding, since the steady load simulation (E31) with respiration near one hundred ten watts per tonne (E21) gives cooling about three hundred fifteen watts, so electrical use with Coefficient of Performance (COP), where COP means cooling per electricity, of two is about one hundred fifty seven watts and three point seven eight kilowatt hours per day, about half a household day and plausible, from a buildable Direct Current (DC), where DC means battery-type power, unit of the Danfoss BD1.4F-FSD Data sheet (E24) class in the DC cooling unit (C5). I am not ready, because pull-down rate and door openings with Chidi and Dalia must fix peak size.
